items.title: The Consciousness Totality, the Sequence of the Three Sets, and the Powers They Unlock

items.zh: 識所行境遍一切故，亦立遍處。復次，修觀行者，先於所緣思惟勝解；次能制伏；既於制伏得自在已，後即於此遍一切處，如其所欲而作勝解；是故此三如是次第。
items.en: Because consciousness's field of activity pervades everything, a totality is also established [on it]. Furthermore, a practitioner of contemplation first generates conviction towards the object, next can subdue it; and once he has gained mastery over subduing it, he then generates conviction that it pervades everywhere, just as he wishes — therefore these three follow in this sequence.

items.zh: 八色遍處善清淨故，能引賢聖勝解神通，及於諸事轉變神通。如其勝解、隨所轉變，皆能成就；又能變作金銀等物，堪有所用。由識遍處善清淨故，便能引發無諍、願智、無礙解等諸勝功德。由空遍處善清淨故，隨其所欲皆轉成空。譬如世間凡鐵金師，初和泥等，未善調練，解脫位亦爾。如善調練，勝處位亦爾。如調練已，隨欲轉變，遍處位亦爾。
items.en: Because the eight form-totalities are well purified, they can elicit the noble ones' conviction-superknowledge and the superknowledge of transforming things: however one is convinced, so it transforms, and all is accomplished; one can even transform things into gold, silver, and the like, fit for use. Because the consciousness-totality is well purified, one can elicit non-contention, the knowledge-of-vows, the analytic knowledges, and other supreme qualities. Because the space-totality is well purified, whatever one wishes all turns into space. Just as a worldly potter or smith, at first mixing the clay, has not yet skilfully worked it — so too the liberation-stage; as he skilfully works it — so too the mastery-stage; as, having worked it, he reshapes it at will — so too the totality-stage.

items.title: The Emptiness Concentration, and the Four Kinds of Emptiness

items.zh: 復次，三三摩地者。云何空三摩地？謂於遠離有情、命者，及養育者、數取趣等，心住一緣。當知空性略有四種。一、觀察空。謂觀察諸法空無常樂，乃至空無我、我所等。二、彼果空。謂不動心解脫，空無貪等一切煩惱。三者、內空。謂於自身空無計我、我所及我慢等一切僻執。四者、外空。謂於五欲空無欲愛。
items.en: Furthermore, the three concentrations. What is the emptiness concentration? Fixing the mind single-pointedly on the absence of a being, a living soul, a nurturer, a transmigrating person, and so on. Know that emptiness is, in brief, of four kinds: first, investigative emptiness — contemplating all phenomena as empty of permanence and pleasure, down to empty of self and mine; second, the emptiness that is its fruit — the unshakable liberation of mind, empty of craving and every affliction; third, internal emptiness — one's own body empty of any reckoning of I, mine, and the conceit of self, and all crooked grasping; fourth, external emptiness — the five desires empty of craving-for-desire.

items.zh: 如說：我已超過一切有色想故，於外空身作證具足住，乃至廣說。此中緣妙欲想，名為色想。此想所起貪欲斷故，說為外空。又修行者，由彼果空，或時作意思惟外空，或時作意思惟內空。由觀察空，或時思惟內外空性；由此力故，心俱證會。
items.en: As it is said: "Because I have transcended all perceptions of form, I dwell complete, directly realising external emptiness in the body," and so on at length. Here the perception conditioned by fine desire is called "perception of form"; because the craving arisen from this perception is severed, it is called "external emptiness." Moreover, a practitioner, by [aspiring to] the fruit-emptiness, sometimes attends to external emptiness and sometimes to internal emptiness; by investigative emptiness he sometimes attends to internal-and-external emptiness — and by this force, the mind realises them together.

items.title: Breaking Through With "the Unwavering," and the Wishlessness Concentration

items.zh: 設復於此內外空性不證會者，便應作意思惟無動。言無動者，謂無常想，或復苦想。如是思惟，便不為彼我慢等動。由彼不為計我、我慢乃至廣說動其心故，便於二空心俱證會。
items.en: Should he still not realise this internal-and-external emptiness, he should attend to and contemplate "the unwavering." "The unwavering" means the perception of impermanence, or the perception of suffering; contemplating thus, he is no longer moved by conceit-of-self and the rest. Because his mind is no longer moved by reckoning a self, by self-conceit, and so on, the mind then realises both emptinesses together.

items.zh: 云何無願心三摩地？謂於五取蘊，思惟無常，或思惟苦，心住一緣。
items.en: What is the wishlessness concentration of mind? Fixing the mind single-pointedly, contemplating the five grasping-aggregates as impermanent, or contemplating them as suffering.

items.title: The Signless Concentration: Neither Low Nor Exalted

items.zh: 云何無相心三摩地？謂即於彼諸取蘊滅，思惟寂靜，心住一緣。如經言：無相心三摩地，不低不昂，乃至廣說。云何名為不低不昂？違順二相不相應故。
items.en: What is the signless concentration of mind? Fixing the mind single-pointedly, contemplating the quiescence [that is] the cessation of those grasping-aggregates. As the sūtra says: "The signless concentration of mind is neither low nor exalted," and so on at length. What is "neither low nor exalted"? Not corresponding to either the repellent or the agreeable sign.

items.zh: 又二因緣，入無相定。一、不思惟一切相故；二、正思惟無相界故。由不思惟一切相故，於彼諸相不厭不壞，惟不加行作意思惟，故名不低。於無相界正思惟故，於彼無相不堅執著，故名不昂。
items.en: Moreover, by two conditions one enters the signless concentration: first, not attending to any sign; second, rightly attending to the signless realm. Because one does not attend to any sign, one neither wearies of nor breaks down those signs, but simply does not apply attention to them — hence "not low." Because one rightly attends to the signless realm yet does not cling firmly to the signless, it is called "not exalted."

items.title: The Signless Concentration's Means and Fruit, and What "Clear Knowing" Yields

items.zh: 此三摩地略有二種。一者、方便，二、方便果。言方便者，數數策勵思擇安立，於彼諸相未能解脫；由隨相識，於時時中擾亂心故。彼復數數自策自勵思擇安立，方能取果，解脫隨相。於此解脫又解脫故，不自策勵思擇而住，是故名為極善解脫。若數策勵思擇安立方得住者，雖名解脫，非善解脫。
items.en: This concentration is, in brief, of two kinds: first, the means; second, the fruit of the means. The means: repeatedly spurring oneself and discerning to establish [the signless], while not yet freed from those signs — because the sign-following consciousness disturbs the mind from time to time. Repeatedly spurring and rousing oneself, discerning to establish it, one is then able to win the fruit and be freed from the sign-following. Because one is freed from this and freed again, one abides without spurring oneself to discern — therefore it is called utterly-good liberation. If one abides only by repeated spurring and discerning-to-establish, though it is called liberation, it is not utterly-good liberation.

items.zh: 又曉了果、曉了功德者，謂煩惱斷究竟故，現法樂住究竟故。又復滅、道俱應曉了。即此二種，隨其次第，名曉了果、曉了功德。又諦現觀、阿羅漢果俱應曉了。
items.en: As for the fruit of clear knowing and the merit of clear knowing: because the severance of affliction is final, and because the pleasant abiding in this very life is final. Moreover, both cessation and path should be clearly known — these two, in sequence, are the fruit of clear knowing and the merit of clear knowing. Moreover, the direct realisation of the truths and the fruit of arhatship should both be clearly known.

items.zh: 於見道位中，名曉了果；於阿羅漢果，名曉了功德。

items.title: Why the Three Doors Bear Their Names — and Why Emptiness Comes First

items.zh: 若於此處無有彼物，由此道理觀之為空，故名空性。即所觀空無可希願，故名無願。觀此遠離一切行相，故名無相。
items.en: Where a thing lacks something, by this principle it is contemplated as empty — hence "emptiness." Because the emptiness contemplated has nothing to be wished for, it is called "wishlessness." Because this is contemplated as removed from all activity-marks, it is called "signlessness."

items.zh: 何故此中先說空性；餘處宣說無常故苦，苦故無我，後方說空？謂若無無我、無常、苦觀終不清淨。要先安住無我之想，從此無間方得無願。是故經言：諸無常想，依無我想而得安住，乃至廣說。彼於無常觀無我已，不生希願，唯願無相，專求出離。故此無間宣說無相。
items.en: Why is emptiness stated first here, whereas elsewhere it is taught "because impermanent, therefore suffering; because suffering, therefore without self," and only afterwards emptiness? Because without [the perception of] no-self, the contemplation of impermanence and suffering is never purified. One must first abide in the perception of no-self, and only then, without interval, does one attain wishlessness. Therefore the sūtra says: "The perceptions of impermanence rest upon the perception of no-self," and so on at length. Having, upon impermanence, contemplated no-self, one generates no wish [for existence] but wishes only for the signless, single-mindedly seeking release — therefore, without interval, signlessness is taught next.

blocks.text: Today's reading completes the liberations, masteries, and totalities, and then explains the three concentrations known as the **gateways of liberation**: emptiness, wishlessness, and signlessness. This passage contains a classical definition of emptiness that Yogācāra regards as the correct one, in contrast to the "wrongly grasped emptiness" of Day 50.

The liberations, masteries, and totalities lead to supernormal powers, the knowledge that arises from resolve, the analytic knowledges, and **non-contention** (無諍), the ability to keep others from conceiving afflictions. Master Cháng Bǎi: an arhat's non-contention aims to keep beings from afflictions; a Buddha's aims at their liberation.

The treatise compares the three stages to a potter. Master Cháng Bǎi's example: visitors at a pottery kiln can make pots, "but however they shape it, it won't look good". The liberations are learning; the masteries, skill; the totalities, mastery.

The **emptiness concentration** (空三摩地) has four kinds: investigative emptiness; its fruit, "the unshakable liberation of mind, empty of craving, hatred, and delusion"; inner emptiness; and outer emptiness. It removes the notions of "a being, a living soul, a nurturer, a transmigrator". Venerable Miào Jìng: "nurturer" is said from the side of cause, "transmigrator" from the side of result.

If inner and outer emptiness are not yet realised, one contemplates "**the unwavering**". Master Cháng Bǎi: contemplating the impermanence or suffering of the body inside and out, so that self-conceit, self-view, and self-love do not arise.

The **wishless concentration** (無願三摩地) does not wish for any conditioned existence, seeing it as suffering. The **signless concentration of mind** (無相心三摩地) attends to no sign. It is "neither low nor exalted": not low, because it neither wearies of nor breaks down signs; not exalted, because it rightly attends to the signless without clinging. Venerable Miào Jìng on what disturbs it: the "sign-following consciousness" is the clinging mind, to which signs keep returning.

Then the classical definition. "Where a thing lacks something, it is seen as empty of that; and what remains there is known as it truly is, as existing." Master Cháng Bǎi gives the *Madhyama Āgama*'s example: saying Migāramātā's hall is empty means it has no cattle or sheep in it, "not that the hall itself is gone".

This is the Yogācāra reading of emptiness in one sentence. The dependent nature is empty *of* the imagined nature (a self, an essence); what remains, the dependent and perfected natures, is real (Day 50). Emptiness is always the absence of something in something.

Elsewhere the order is impermanence, suffering, non-self, then emptiness. Here emptiness comes first, "because without the perception of non-self, the contemplation of impermanence and suffering is never purified". One must first abide in non-self, then see impermanence and suffering without a self to suffer them.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe the sequence of liberations, masteries, and totalities?
options: the eight liberations come first, eliciting the eight masteries, which elicit the ten totalities — each earlier elicits the later
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The eight liberations come first, then they bring forth the eight masteries, which bring forth the ten totalities — the earlier elicits the later." The text: first conviction, then subdual, then pervasive conviction at will.

quiz.q: The consciousness totality elicits non-contention. How does an arhat's non-contention differ from a buddha's, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the arhat aims to keep beings from giving rise to affliction; the Buddha aims at whether beings are liberated
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "A great arhat's non-contention differs from a buddha's: the arhat aims at keeping beings from arising afflictions; the Buddha aims at whether beings can be saved." Subhūti is the famous example. Venerable Miào Jìng: he avoids being the cause of another's affliction.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what four kinds of emptiness are there?
options: investigative emptiness, its fruit, internal emptiness, external emptiness
quiz.why: "First, investigative emptiness …; second, the emptiness that is its fruit — the unshakable liberation of mind, empty of craving and every affliction; third, internal emptiness …; fourth, external emptiness — the five desires empty of craving." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is emptiness to cultivate, the second to realise.

quiz.q: If internal-external emptiness isn't realised, one should contemplate "the unwavering." What is it, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: contemplating impermanence or suffering in body inner and outer — so one has no self-conceit, self-view, self-love, or self-delusion towards the aggregates
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The unwavering means contemplating impermanence or suffering of the inner and outer body; doing so constantly, one has no self-conceit, self-view, self-love, or self-delusion towards the aggregates." The text: "'The unwavering' means the perception of impermanence, or the perception of suffering."

quiz.q: Why is the signless concentration "neither low nor exalted," per the treatise?
options: not attending to signs, neither wearying of nor breaking them — not low; rightly attending to the signless without clinging — not exalted
quiz.why: "Because one does not attend to any sign, one neither wearies of nor breaks down those signs … hence 'not low.' Because one rightly attends to the signless realm yet does not cling firmly to the signless, it is called 'not exalted.'" Venerable Miào Jìng: repellent and agreeable are both signs.

quiz.q: The text says "where a thing lacks something, it is seen as empty." What Madhyama Āgama example does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: saying Migāramātā's hall is empty means it lacks cattle and sheep, not that the hall itself is gone
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Saying Migāramātā's hall is empty means there are no cattle or sheep in it — not that the hall itself doesn't exist." Venerable Miào Jìng: the aggregates lack a self, but the aggregates still exist.

quiz.q: Elsewhere impermanence, suffering, no-self come before emptiness; why is emptiness first here?
options: without no-self, contemplation of impermanence and suffering is never purified — one must first abide in no-self, then wishlessness follows
quiz.why: "Because without the perception of no-self, the contemplation of impermanence and suffering is never purified. One must first abide in the perception of no-self, and only then, without interval, does one attain wishlessness." Venerable Miào Jìng: emptiness of dharmas without no-self leaves one ordinary.
